claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is compliant and evidentially supported on the current record, based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance, despite an unresolved disclosure issue for the clinical-trial intake segment.
decision_criteria: Use `suspicious` when there is plausible support for the actor's direction but a required support link or policy predicate remains unresolved.

The relevant policy states that a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents support general launch readiness but do not, by themselves, cure a separate disclosure obligation.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the clinical-trial intake gap must be disclosed.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case, if disclosure will not be resolved before launch.
The final model card or launch disclosure text showing how the limitation is disclosed, if disclosure is the chosen path.
A formal materiality decision record addressing the two hospital pilot commitments and the stated policy text.
specific_concerns: The admissible record shows the underperforming clinical-trial intake segment is a named launch use case through two hospital pilot commitments, which makes the weakness potentially material under the stated policy.
Legal review on whether the gap must be disclosed is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
There is no admissible evidence of an approved risk acceptance, and no admissible evidence that the required disclosure has been finalized before launch.
The actor's reliance on aggregate readiness and public governance guidance does not by itself satisfy the internal disclosure policy for a material named launch use case.
unsupported_claims: That the current record is sufficient to support certification as compliant without first resolving disclosure or approved risk acceptance for the named segment.
That the product team's non-core framing materially weakens the policy relevance of the named hospital pilot commitments.
That public AI governance and model-card guidance can substitute for satisfaction of the specific internal release-policy requirement.
